transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Yeah, thanks. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and I have to do these reports, but I keep copying the wrong numbers from the team dashboard. Which, honestly, the new dashboard software they make us use is just awful. They updated it last month and now everything is in this weird tiny font, and my buddy Dave—he's over in IT—told me they bought the absolute cheapest package available. Typical corporate, you know? Always cutting corners. Dave's actually the guy who helped me replace the alternator on my truck last weekend, which was a whole nightmare on its own because the auto shop sent the wrong part twice... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, work. Yeah, so I'll be doing the reports, and I'll just completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check off. Like, totally skip it, even when I swear I just went over the whole thing and thought it was fine. It's getting pretty frustrating.
Have you noticed these kinds of attention and focus problems since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started more recently?

Yeah, it's definitely not a new thing. I was like this as a kid, too. My mom actually still talks about it—she kept all these old teacher notes from elementary school. They were always saying how I rushed through my work, lost my homework, talked out of turn, and just couldn't stay seated without them constantly reminding me. 

She actually just found a whole box of those old notes when she was packing for her move. She's relocating down to Florida next month, right near Tampa. Which is wild to me because she absolutely hates the heat. I keep telling her the humidity is gonna be brutal, especially in August. I went down there a few years ago for a bachelor party—my buddy Steve's, actually, he's the one who works in logistics now—and man, we went deep-sea fishing and I got so sunburned I couldn't wear a real shirt for three days. The boat captain was this crazy old guy who just kept telling us these wild stories about catching sharks in the 80s and how the regulations ruined everything... um... sorry, what did you ask me? Did I answer the question?
Aside from the attention issues, do you often feel restless, feel the need to move around, or find yourself interrupting others or blurting things out?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, sitting through a long meeting is just... it feels like my whole body is buzzing inside, you know? I literally can't just sit there. I have to shift around, or I'm constantly tapping my foot, or I just make up some excuse to get up and grab a coffee or go to the bathroom. Which actually reminds me, the coffee machine in our breakroom has been broken for like two weeks. It's one of those fancy Keurig ones, but somebody jammed a non-compatible pod in there, and now it just spits out hot water everywhere. My buddy Dave from IT—yeah, same Dave—tried to fix it, but he said the internal pump is completely shot. So now we all have to walk down the street to this little cafe, which is fine, but they charge like six bucks for a regular drip coffee. Six bucks! I remember when you could get a coffee and a donut for two dollars. My grandpa used to take me to this old diner every Sunday morning when I was a kid, and he'd always get a black coffee and a cruller. He swore by those crullers. Said the place had the best ones in the state, but they closed down back in... wait. I lost my train of thought again. Sorry. What was I talking about? Oh, right, the meetings and moving around. Yeah, I just can't sit still for very long without feeling like I'm gonna jump out of my skin.
Aside from work, do these same kinds of problems—like losing focus, restlessness, or impulsivity—also cause noticeable difficulties in your home life or personal relationships?

Yeah, it definitely spills over. I mean, at work, it's actually gotten to the point where my manager put it in my formal review, which was pretty embarrassing. But at home, it's honestly just as bad, if not worse. It causes a lot of arguments because my wife feels like she just can't count on me to follow through on things. Like, she'll ask me to pick up the dry cleaning, and I'll completely forget because I decided to stop at the hardware store to look at power washers. I've been wanting to pressure wash the deck before winter hits. The wood is starting to look really gray and weathered, you know? My neighbor, Greg, he rented one of those heavy-duty commercial washers last weekend and did his whole driveway in like two hours. It looked brand new. He was out there with the safety goggles and the big rubber boots, looking like he was about to clean up a hazardous waste spill. Greg's a funny guy, though. He's an accountant but he's obsessed with lawn care. He spends more time edging his grass than he does with his kids, I swear. He's got this zero-turn mower that he treats like a sports car... um... wait. Why was I talking about Greg? 

Oh, right, the problems at home. Yeah, so it just adds to the conflict because I don't follow through, and then people get mad at me. It's just really frustrating for everyone.
